title: Compliance thoughtstream — control gaps & evidence mapping
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for current SOC2-ish prep work. Not final. Dumping assumptions, open questions, and a lightweight evidence map so I can hand off to Marco/Evelyn next week.

Context notes (short):
- Customer asks during onboarding repeatedly focus on access logs and data isolation. We need consolidated evidence for: access provisioning, key rotation, network segmentation, and incident logging.
- We have bits scattered: audit logs in GCP Cloud Logging, KMS rotation docs in confluence, a handful of runbooks in /infra repo.
- Goal: turn this into a ~2-page evidence bundle + a simple control matrix for external auditor by end of Q1 (stretch).

Assumptions I am making (validate):
- Dedicated and Private customers count as the same trust domain for controls that apply to Redwood-managed control plane.
- Some infra elements are covered by cloud provider shared-responsibility (need to call out).

Open risk/questions (to triage):
- Who owns proof of key rotation for on-prem HSMs? (we have KMS rotation logs for cloud, different story for on-prem customers)
- Are ephemeral worker nodes used anywhere that create gaps in host-hardening evidence? (I saw notes in infra ticket #TRUST-158)
- Retention: audit logs currently retained 90 days by default. Need to decide if we push to 1 year for enterprise customers or archive strategy.
- Incident playbooks: do we have an 'executive notification' artifact that matches auditor expectations? I can find runbooks but not the matrix that maps severity->notify list.

Quick control mapping brainstorm (very rough):
- Access provisioning (identity lifecycle): evidence = SCIM logs (okta->RBAC), onboarding ticket proof, provisioning playbook (confluence), last-12-months user access review artifact.
- Network segmentation (private deployments): evidence = VPC diagrams, firewall rule exports (gcloud compute firewall-rules list), sample config for private deployment, pen-test summary for network controls.
- Key management: evidence = KMS key policies, rotation logs, KMS IAM bindings, HSM attestation for on-prem (if exists), KMS backup snapshot policy.
- Logging & monitoring: evidence = Cloud Logging exports, log retention policy, sample incident log (sanitized), alerting rules (PagerDuty integration doc).
- Change control: evidence = PR merge history (github PRs with approvals), deploy playbook, CD pipeline gated approvals, emergency rollback checklist.

Mini-evidence matrix (text):
Control | Candidate artifact(s) | Current owner | Gaps
Access lifecycle | okta SCIM audit + onboarding tickets | IDP team (Evelyn) | need consolidated access review report
KMS rotation | cloud KMS rotation logs | infra (Marco) | on-prem HSM attestation missing
Logging retention | Cloud Logging export config | observability | retention only 90d default
Change control | github PRs + CODEOWNERS | platform-eng | ad-hoc approvals for infra repo still happening

Immediate action ideas (pick low-hanging fruit):
- Script to export last-12-months SCIM provisioning events and pivot by user (ticket: JIRA-TRUST-4321). Owner: Evelyn. ETA: 1 week.
- Snapshot of KMS rotation events for last 6 months, include IAM bindings. Owner: Marco. ETA: 4 days.
- Draft single-page "evidence index" (one-line mapping of control->artifact URL) to hand to auditor. I can draft. Owner: Kaiya. ETA: 3 days.
- Decide retention policy escalation: propose a policy doc to move enterprise customers' logs to cold storage for 1 year. Liaise with finance for cost estimate.

Notes to self / reminders: 
- Sanitize any sample logs before sharing externally. Use mapping script that masks user ids.
- Keep a separate folder for 'sensitive evidence' that requires access gating.
- Cross-check confluence pages for inconsistent language: e.g., some pages call it 'rotation schedule', others 'rekeying' — unify terminology.

Potential blockers: 
- On-prem HSM owners may be customers; we can only request attestation, not produce. Need guidance on acceptable auditor evidence (customer-supplied attestation vs. Redwood responsibility).
- Some 'evidence' is ephemeral (PRs get squashed) — prefer stable exports/artifacts rather than live links.

Questions for the next triage meeting with Marco/Evelyn:
1) Which controls are priority for 3rd party auditors vs. internal stakeholders?
2) Can platform-eng commit to providing 6 months of KMS rotation logs within sprint 14?
3) Do we want to centralize evidence in a gated S3 bucket and share signed read-only links to auditors?

Quick todo (my own):
- Draft the evidence index (today).
- Open a workspace in confluence 'trust/evidence-bucket' and start populating artifacts with short notes (tomorrow).
- Add a checklist for log sanitization to the infra repo.

Random brainstorming (may be useful):
- Could we build a tiny 'evidence exporter' that collects PR metadata, SCIM exports, KMS rotation events and zips them with a digest? One-off tool for audits. Low priority but useful.
- Consider adding 'auditor mode' to console that shows redacted examples of logs for demo.

End of notes.

(If you are reading this later: look at ticket JIRA-TRUST-4321 and confluence 'attestation-plan' for the latest structured checklist.)
